title: K-Means Clustering
description: K-Means: Unsupervised clustering! Group data into K clusters. Algorithm: (1) Initialize K centroids randomly. (2) Assign each point to nearest centroid. (3) Update centroids (mean of assigned points). (4) Repeat until convergence. Simple, fast, scalable. Hyperparameter: K (number of clusters) - choose via elbow method, silhouette score. Applications: Customer segmentation, image compression, anomaly detection. Limitations: Assumes spherical clusters, sensitive to initialization (use k-means++), needs to specify K beforehand.

content.level0_basic: K-Means: Group similar data points! Example: Customer segmentation (high/medium/low spenders). Algorithm: (1) Pick K random points as cluster centers. (2) Assign each point to nearest center. (3) Move centers to average of their points. (4) Repeat until stable. Simple! Choose K: Elbow method (plot error vs K, find 'elbow'). Fast: O(n·K·iterations). Works well when clusters are round/spherical. Fails on weird shapes (moons, rings). k-means++: Better initialization (not fully random).
content.level1_beginner:
**K-Means Algorithm:**

```
1. Initialize K centroids (k-means++ or random)
2. Repeat until convergence:
   a. Assignment: Each point → nearest centroid
   b. Update: Move centroid to mean of assigned points
3. Converged when centroids don't move
```

**Distance:** Euclidean typically
**Objective:** Minimize within-cluster sum of squares (WCSS)
**Initialization:** k-means++ (smart seeding)
**Choosing K:** Elbow method, silhouette score
content.level2_application:
**Scikit-learn:**

```python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init='k-means++', random_state=42)
kmeans.fit(X)

labels = kmeans.labels_
centers = kmeans.cluster_centers_
inertia = kmeans.inertia_  # WCSS

plt.scatter(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], c=labels)
plt.scatter(centers[:, 0], centers[:, 1], marker='X', s=200, c='red')
plt.show()
```
content.level3_advanced:
**Elbow Method:**

```python
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 11):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

plt.plot(range(1, 11), inertias, marker='o')
plt.xlabel('K')
plt.ylabel('Inertia')
plt.title('Elbow Method')
plt.show()
```

whatIsIt: K-Means: Partitional clustering. Assigns each point to one of K clusters. Minimizes within-cluster sum of squared distances (WCSS). Iterative: Assignment step (Voronoi diagram), update step (centroid = mean). Converges to local minimum. k-means++: Smart initialization reduces bad local minima. Hard clustering (each point one cluster). Soft variant: Fuzzy c-means.
whyNeeded: Why clustering: Find natural groups in unlabeled data! Applications: (1) Customer segmentation (marketing). (2) Image compression (color quantization). (3) Document clustering (topic discovery). (4) Anomaly detection (points far from all clusters). (5) Feature engineering (cluster membership as feature). K-Means advantages: Simple, fast O(n·K·i), scales well. Disadvantages: Assumes spherical clusters, sensitive to outliers, needs K beforehand.
realWorldAnalogy: K-Means = Friend groups! High school: K groups (jocks, nerds, artists, etc.). Algorithm: (1) Seed: Pick K random 'leaders'. (2) Assignment: Each person joins nearest leader's group. (3) Update: Each group's new 'leader' = average personality of group. (4) Repeat: People might switch groups as leaders change. Converge: Stable groups! Choosing K: Too few (K=2, jocks vs everyone) → oversimplified. Too many (K=50) → overfitted. Elbow: Find natural number of groups. Spherical assumption: Groups are 'round' (similar sizes, shapes). Fails if weird shapes!

stepByStep: a. Assign each point to nearest centroid
b. Update each centroid to mean of assigned points
algorithm.complexity: O(n·K·i·d) where n=samples, K=clusters, i=iterations (typically <100), d=dimensions. Mini-batch: O(b·K·i·d) where b=batch size. Space: O(n·d + K·d).

codeExamples.title: Basic K-Means
codeExamples.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(300, 2)
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
kmeans.fit(X)

print(f'Labels: {kmeans.labels_[:10]}')
print(f'Centers: {kmeans.cluster_centers_}')
print(f'Inertia: {kmeans.inertia_:.2f}')

codeExamples.title: Elbow Method
codeExamples.code:
inertias = []
for k in range(1, 11):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k)
    km.fit(X)
    inertias.append(km.inertia_)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(range(1, 11), inertias, 'o-')
plt.xlabel('K')
plt.ylabel('Inertia')
plt.title('Elbow Method')
plt.show()

codeExamples.title: Silhouette Score
codeExamples.code:
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

for k in range(2, 11):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k)
    labels = km.fit_predict(X)
    score = silhouette_score(X, labels)
    print(f'K={k}: Silhouette={score:.3f}')

codeExamples.title: Visualization
codeExamples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X)
centers = kmeans.cluster_centers_

plt.scatter(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], c=labels, cmap='viridis', alpha=0.5)
plt.scatter(centers[:, 0], centers[:, 1], c='red', marker='X', s=200, edgecolors='black')
plt.title('K-Means Clustering')
plt.show()

codeExamples.title: Mini-Batch K-Means
codeExamples.code:
from sklearn.cluster import MiniBatchKMeans
import time

# Large dataset
X_large = np.random.randn(100000, 50)

start = time.time()
mbkm = MiniBatchKMeans(n_clusters=10, batch_size=1000)
mbkm.fit(X_large)
print(f'Mini-batch time: {time.time()-start:.2f}s')

start = time.time()
km = KMeans(n_clusters=10)
km.fit(X_large)
print(f'Regular time: {time.time()-start:.2f}s')

codeExamples.title: Image Compression
codeExamples.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

# Load image
img = Image.open('image.jpg')
img_array = np.array(img)
pixels = img_array.reshape(-1, 3)  # Flatten to (n_pixels, 3)

# Cluster colors
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=16)  # 16 colors only
kmeans.fit(pixels)

# Replace with cluster centers
compressed = kmeans.cluster_centers_[kmeans.labels_]
compressed_img = compressed.reshape(img_array.shape).astype('uint8')

Image.fromarray(compressed_img).save('compressed.jpg')
print('Image compressed from 16M to 16 colors!')

quiz.question: K-Means'in amacı nedir?
options: Minimize within-cluster sum of squares: Group similar points together!
quiz.explanation: K-Means objective: Minimize WCSS (within-cluster sum of squared distances). Each point should be close to its cluster centroid. Iteratively improves: Assignment (move points) + Update (move centroids). Converges to local minimum. Unsupervised: No labels needed!

quiz.question: k-means++ neden kullanılır?
options: Better initialization: Spreads initial centroids, avoids bad local minima
quiz.explanation: k-means++: Smart initialization! Instead of random centroids, spreads them out. Picks first random, then picks next far from existing ones. Result: Better starting point → better final clusters, faster convergence. Sklearn default! Without: Can get stuck in bad local minimum.

quiz.question: Elbow method ne işe yarar?
options: Find optimal K: Plot inertia vs K, look for 'elbow' point!
quiz.explanation: Elbow method: Choose K! Plot inertia (WCSS) vs K. Inertia always decreases with more K. Look for 'elbow': Point where decrease slows. Before elbow: Adding clusters helps a lot. After: Diminishing returns. Not always clear elbow! Alternatives: Silhouette score, domain knowledge.

quiz.question: K-Means hangi cluster şekillerinde başarısız?
quiz.explanation: K-Means assumes: Spherical clusters, similar sizes. Fails on: (1) Non-convex shapes (moons, crescents). (2) Different densities. (3) Elongated clusters. (4) Nested structures (ring inside ring). Why: Uses Euclidean distance, finds circular regions. Alternatives: DBSCAN (density), hierarchical (any shape), GMM (elliptical).

quiz.question: Inertia (WCSS) nedir?
options: Sum of squared distances from points to their centroids: Clustering quality!
quiz.explanation: Inertia = WCSS = Σ||x - μ_cluster||². Lower = better clustering (points closer to centroids). Always decreases with more K! K=n → inertia=0 (each point its own cluster). Not comparable across datasets. Use: Track convergence, elbow method. Alternative: Silhouette (compares to other clusters).

quiz.question: Mini-Batch K-Means'in avantajı?
options: Much faster: Uses random batches, scales to millions of samples!
quiz.explanation: Mini-Batch K-Means: Sample random batch, update centroids, repeat. Much faster! 10-100× speedup on large data. Slight accuracy loss (~1-2%). Essential for: Large datasets (>100k samples), streaming data, online learning. Regular K-Means: Recomputes all distances each iteration → slow. Mini-batch: Stochastic, faster convergence.

commonMistakes.why: K-Means uses Euclidean distance! Different scales → large-scale features dominate clustering.
commonMistakes.fix: Always StandardScaler before K-Means! Critical for good results. Otherwise: Clustering based on scale, not patterns.

commonMistakes.why: K=1: Everything one cluster (useless). Random K: No validation. Suboptimal clusters.
commonMistakes.fix: Use elbow method or silhouette score to choose K! Or domain knowledge. Try range (2-10), evaluate quality.

commonMistakes.why: K-Means converges to local minimum! Random init → different results each time. Might be bad local min.
commonMistakes.fix: Use init='k-means++' (sklearn default) or multiple random initializations (n_init=10). Take best result. More stable!

commonMistakes.why: Default max_iter=300. Large datasets: Might not converge. Bad clusters, wasted computation.
commonMistakes.fix: Check: kmeans.n_iter_. If equals max_iter: Didn't converge! Increase max_iter or check data quality.

commonMistakes.why: K-Means assumes spherical! Moons, rings, elongated → fails completely. Meaningless clusters.
commonMistakes.fix: Check data shape first! Non-spherical: Use DBSCAN, hierarchical, or GMM. K-Means: Only when clusters roughly round.

commonMistakes.why: Outliers pull centroids! Distort clusters. One outlier can ruin entire cluster.
commonMistakes.fix: Detect and remove outliers first! Or use robust methods (DBSCAN handles outliers). Or increase K to isolate outliers in own cluster.

commonMistakes.why: Inertia scale-dependent! Dataset A: inertia=100 'good'. Dataset B: inertia=100 might be bad. Not comparable!
commonMistakes.fix: Don't compare absolute inertia! Use: (1) Silhouette score (normalized). (2) Within-dataset comparisons (elbow). (3) Domain validation.
